penz_home1_mum.text: Dydh da! That is 'good day' in Cornish. Come in, kettle's on dreckly.
Dreckly is Cornish for 'some time, maybe, no rush'. It is not the same as 'now'.
Chipgulls will take the pasty right out of your hand. Hold it tight and glare.
My grandson says 'meur ras' for thank you. I taught him that. And the cat.

then.text: Crimp's on the side, not the top. Want to borrow the range?

else.text: Dreckly, my lover, dreckly. Oh, you're not the man about the boiler.
You've the look of someone who picks seaweed off the beach and doesn't know what to do with it.
Here. A proper pasty, a little creel for the Brook lot, and how to dress a hag stone. My nan's ways. Don't tell the Tourist Board.
Pop in whenever you've got the makings. You can use my kitchen.
